question: For order 423, identify the product IDs, aisles, and positions from which to pick the exact quantities needed for each order line, ensuring that the total picked quantity for each product matches the cumulative quantities ordered without exceeding the available inventory in warehouse 1. Calculate the quantities to be picked from each location by prioritizing inventory with earlier purchased dates and smaller quantities, and ensure that picking respects the sequence and cumulative quantities of the order lines for products with multiple entries.
sql:
WITH order_lines AS (
    SELECT order_id, product_id, qty as total_needed, 
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY id) as line_seq
    FROM orderlines 
    WHERE order_id = 423
),
inventory_available AS (
    SELECT i.id as inv_id, i.product_id, i.location_id, i.purchase_id, i.qty as available_qty, 
           p.purchased, l.warehouse, l.aisle, l.position
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
      AND i.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_lines)
),
pick_base AS (
    SELECT 
        ol.product_id,
        ol.total_needed,
        ia.inv_id,
        ia.location_id,
        ia.warehouse,
        ia.aisle,
        ia.position,
        ia.purchased,
        ia.available_qty,
        SUM(ia.available_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY ia.purchased, ia.available_qty ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as cum_available
    FROM order_lines ol
    JOIN inventory_available ia ON ol.product_id = ia.product_id
),
pick_with_remaining AS (
    SELECT *,
        COALESCE(LAG(cum_available) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased, available_qty), 0) as prev_cum_available
    FROM pick_base
),
pick_calc AS (
    SELECT 
        product_id,
        aisle,
        position,
        GREATEST(0, LEAST(available_qty, total_needed - prev_cum_available)) as picked_qty
    FROM pick_with_remaining
)
SELECT 
    product_id,
    aisle,
    position,
    picked_qty
FROM pick_calc
WHERE picked_qty > 0
ORDER BY product_id, picked_qty DESC

{"sql": "WITH order_lines AS (
    SELECT order_id, product_id, qty as total_needed, 
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY id) as line_seq
    FROM orderlines 
    WHERE order_id = 423
),
inventory_available AS (
    SELECT i.id as inv_id, i.product_id, i.location_id, i.purchase_id, i.qty as available_qty, 
           p.purchased, l.warehouse, l.aisle, l.position
    FROM inventory i
    JOIN locations l ON i.location_id = l.id
    JOIN purchases p ON i.purchase_id = p.id
    WHERE l.warehouse = 1
      AND i.product_id IN (SELECT product_id FROM order_lines)
),
pick_base AS (
    SELECT 
        ol.product_id,
        ol.total_needed,
        ia.inv_id,
        ia.location_id,
        ia.warehouse,
        ia.aisle,
        ia.position,
        ia.purchased,
        ia.available_qty,
        SUM(ia.available_qty) OVER (PARTITION BY ol.product_id ORDER BY ia.purchased, ia.available_qty ROWS UNBOUNDED PRECEDING) as cum_available
    FROM order_lines ol
    JOIN inventory_available ia ON ol.product_id = ia.product_id
),
pick_with_remaining AS (
    SELECT *,
        LAG(cum_available) OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY purchased, available_qty) as prev_cum_available
    FROM pick_base
)
SELECT 
    product_id,
    inv_id,
    location_id,
    warehouse,
    aisle,
    position,
    purchased,
    available_qty,
    cum_available,
    prev_cum_available,
    total_needed,
    CASE 
        WHEN prev_cum_available IS NULL THEN LEAST(available_qty, total_needed)
        WHEN cum_available <= total_needed THEN available_qty
        ELSE total_needed - prev_cum_available
    END as picked_qty
FROM pick_with_remaining
ORDER BY product_id, purchased, available_qty"}
